artifacts.synopsis: TE John Hardie appealed his conviction and indefinite suspension by Metro Atlanta Presbytery's judicial commission, raising seventeen specifications of error under six categories including procedural irregularities, improper evidence, refusal of indulgence, prejudice, and disproportionate censure. The SJC denied the appeal, finding no clear error in MAP's proceedings and upholding the indefinite suspension.

artifacts.title: Spann v. Oak Mountain Presbyterian Church
artifacts.synopsis: Susan Elizabeth Spann filed an appeal alleging Oak Mountain Presbyterian Church committed excommunication without process and spiritual abuse, but the SJC dismissed the appeal as premature because there was no record of a judicial decision by OMPC nor any prior appeal to Evangel Presbytery as required by BCO 42-2. The SJC requested that Evangel Presbytery direct OMPC to provide a written response to Ms. Spann's concerns.

artifacts.synopsis: The Standing Judicial Commission sustained the complaint of TE Jones et al. against Louisiana Presbytery, finding that LAP erred in two ways: first, in failing to apply the correct constitutional standard for determining whether TE Wilkins had differences with the Westminster Standards (differences need not involve overt contradiction or denial, but can arise from different interpretations of wording or biblical exegesis); and second, in failing to adequately investigate and evaluate such differences as required by RAO 16-3(e)(5), thereby neglecting its duty to condemn erroneous opinions that injure the peace or purity of the church.

artifacts.synopsis: Westminster Presbytery was found to have erred in its BCO 31-2 investigation of secret taping by TE Frank Smith by failing to obtain full witness testimony and investigate legal ramifications; case remanded. The court found no proof of partiality and declined to require establishment of unbiblical criteria for secret taping. Vote: 18 concurring, 1 dissenting (RE Frederick Neikirk), 2 recused, 1 abstained, 2 absent.

artifacts.title: Mt. Carmel Session v. New Jersey Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: The Mt. Carmel Session complained that New Jersey Presbytery erred by adopting a resolution of Affirmations and Denials Regarding the Interpretation of Genesis One that denied the 24-hour-day view as the only acceptable interpretation. The SJC majority denied the complaint (12-9), holding that NJP acted within its constitutional authority under BCO 11-4 to resolve questions of doctrine, consistent with prior General Assembly decisions allowing latitude on creation-day interpretation; a minority report was filed and the case was referred to the 26th General Assembly for final disposition.

artifacts.title: Scope and duration of BCO debate prohibitions during a complaint

matches.evidence: BCO prohibitions on debate apply only to the specific matter complained, only until final adjudication, and to all members of the lower court — expiring upon final resolution.
